correctness.rationale: Each reverse preimage from a singleton that occurs in a shortest reset word must genuinely expand under b/c or translate under inverse a; otherwise that letter can be removed using monotonicity. The sets remain circular arcs. Every step decrements their left endpoint by one and only sites 0,n-1 support expansion, with precisely one forced label per site. Exactly n-1 expansions must occupy the shortest span of a periodic alternating-gap pattern, giving (n-2) floor(n/2)+1 and respectively one or two minimum spans. Reversing the forced paths gives the displayed words. Boundary n=2 and all parities are covered. A standalone exhaustive subset BFS checked n=2..15; complete optimal-word reconstruction n=2..12; independent event arithmetic n=2..50. Finite tests are checks only.

value.rationale: For a natural, explicitly specified 3-letter extension of the extremal Černý family, adding a second neighboring rank-(n-1) collapse lowers the reset threshold from (n-1)^2 to an exact half-quadratic law. Determining the unique/two optimal reset words is a structural classification and exposes a parity-dependent rigidity not implied by general upper bounds or early-rank profile results; it supplies benchmark instances for studying alphabet extensions and synchronization complexity.
